investigation.multipart_fixture_result: CONSTRUCTED + TRACED (not just code-read). Fixture: 3-part series, p1 state=complete/series_final=false/expires_at_epoch in past, p2 state=complete/series_final=false/not expired, p3 state=queued (non-terminal). series_is_complete(root,'s3') returned False -> part 1 PROTECTED. End-to-end trace through main() sections 1-2 confirms the same: the bug-49 guard fires in BOTH the release loop (section 1) and the folder-only loop (section 2) using identical inputs (timing from the job's own status.json + series_is_complete over disk folders), so the two checks cannot disagree for the same job. Release deletion in section 1 is inline, but series_is_complete reads only jobs/<id>/status.json folders via list_job_ids_from_disk (never releases), and folder rmtree is deferred to section 4 after expired_job_ids is final, so inline release deletion cannot change a later sibling's protection verdict. Verified: PROTECT/EXPIRED decisions in the post-fix workflow run logs are internally consistent with this.

investigation.confirmed_root_cause: CONFIRMED VIA GIT ARCHAEOLOGY + ACTUAL WORKFLOW RUN LOGS (api.github.com actions/runs/<id>/logs): the operator-observed cascades were produced by the PRE-bug-66 code, not by the current pipeline/cleanup/expired.py. The last incomplete-series cascade is cleanup commit 1d6ad63 (2026-08-29 18:23:52Z, run 33268138682), which deleted manual-1787970449255 (series-1787970477573 part 1) AND series-1787970477573-p2 — a 2-part series whose parts were both terminal but NEITHER marked is_final (part 3 never started). The run log shows 'EXPIRED job=series-1787970477573-p2' with NO 'PROTECT' line for either part. The bug-66 fix commit e81ac72 (series_is_complete must require an is_final part) landed at 2026-08-29 19:10:24Z — 47 minutes AFTER that run. Pre-fix series_is_complete treated 'all existing parts terminal' as complete (the is_final flag was surfaced by read_job_timing for bug-49 but never consumed), so when the earliest part expired, every terminal sibling was reaped with it — exactly the reported symptom. Earlier cascades fit the same pattern: 343446f (2026-08-29 15:01:47Z, run 33259122992, pre-fix code) reaped series-1787949354863-p2 in the SAME run that reaped its own part 1 (manual-1787949332118) — p2's expires_at (1788011928) was already past because its 12h TTL was anchored at creation; run 33259122992's log proves the bug-49 PROTECT lines existed but the no-is_final pre-fix logic still returned 'complete'. POST-fix verification: every cleanup commit after e81ac72 (0b956eb, db3aeb1, 4ee2a8a, f8bbe58, d819118, 3712302) deleted only (a) parts of genuinely finished series whose sibling was terminal AND is_final=true (series-1787978275321 p1+p2 where p2 is_final=true; series-1788166763252 p1 where live p2 is is_final=true/complete — both legitimate per design), or (b) orphan folders with no status.json at all (manual-1788086523193, manual-1788116356288 — folder contained only source.torrent; legacy 'no readable status = expired' rule, no series guard can apply to a job whose identity is unreadable), or (c) non-series jobs. All five mandated scenario fixtures traced against the CURRENT code return the correct (protected) outcome, including the single-part-pending-next scenario. CONCLUSION: the defect the operator reports was real, was root-caused as bug-66, and is already fixed in the current source; no new code change is warranted. Remediation for this initiative = permanent regression tests pinning every traced scenario (including the exact operator scenario) so any future regression of the guard fails the suite, plus this written evidence trail. Human review item: orphan folders without status.json are reaped unconditionally (legacy rule); if the operator wants series-aware protection to extend to unreadable folders, that is a behavior change beyond this contract's 'missing/unknown = protect' scope for series membership (unreadable folder has no readable series_id to protect by).

fix.approach: No source change to pipeline/cleanup/expired.py: the investigation proved with workflow-run-log evidence that the current bug-49 + bug-66 guard already implements exactly the contract's standard (missing/unknown = protect, don't reap) and that every operator-observed cascade predates the bug-66 fix e81ac72. Changing the code would risk weakening correct behavior — the fix requirement ('fix precisely what the investigation confirms') resolves to: lock the confirmed-correct behavior in with permanent regression tests for every traced scenario, so a future regression of the guard is caught by the suite instead of by the operator losing series parts. Added class SeriesTTLOperatorScenarios (8 tests) to pipeline/tests/test_cleanup.py.

human_review_items: Orphan job folders with no status.json (only source.torrent, e.g. manual-1788086523193) are reaped as 'no readable timing -> expired' with no series protection possible (no readable series_id).
